questions.prompt: An OAuth client uses PKCE with S256. What binds the token exchange to its authorization request?

sources.title: RFC 7636: Proof Key for Code Exchange by OAuth Public Clients
sources.claim: The authorization request sends a challenge derived from a secret verifier. At exchange the server checks the verifier transformation against that challenge. The challenge is not an access token or a password hash, and the raw verifier is not sent at the first step.

questions.explanation: The authorization request sends a challenge derived from a secret verifier. At exchange the server checks the verifier transformation against that challenge. The challenge is not an access token or a password hash, and the raw verifier is not sent at the first step.

choices.text: The client sends the challenge as the access token without a token exchange.
The server compares the transformed verifier to the saved challenge.
The server compares the authorization code directly to the password hash.
The client publishes the raw verifier in the initial authorization request.

questions.prompt: An Express endpoint parses a Stripe webhook as JSON and then serializes the object before verifying its signature. Why can verification fail?

sources.title: Stripe: Receive Stripe events in your webhook endpoint
sources.claim: Stripe signs the raw payload; parser/serializer changes can change its bytes. Verification does not use only event type or require reserialization. Preserve the original body rather than impose a universal JSON field order.

questions.explanation: Stripe signs the raw payload; parser/serializer changes can change its bytes. Verification does not use only event type or require reserialization. Preserve the original body rather than impose a universal JSON field order.

choices.text: Verification uses only the parsed event type and ignores the request body.
Verification expects every request to contain the same whitespace and field order.
Verification needs the original raw request body.
Verification treats JSON serialization as a required canonicalization step.

questions.prompt: A service stores login passwords. Which storage practices follow OWASP guidance? Select all that apply.

sources.title: OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet
sources.claim: A and B resist offline guessing and precomputed attacks. E permits cost upgrades after successful verification. C is false because fast hashes enable rapid guesses. D is false because excessive cost can exhaust server resources; measure it.

questions.explanation: A and B resist offline guessing and precomputed attacks. E permits cost upgrades after successful verification. C is false because fast hashes enable rapid guesses. D is false because excessive cost can exhaust server resources; measure it.

choices.text: Use a slow password-hashing algorithm with a suitable work factor.
Use a unique salt for each stored password hash.
Use fast SHA-256 alone because rapid verification also prevents guessing.
Increase cost without benchmarking because higher cost cannot harm availability.
Rehash at login when the stored work factor needs upgrading.

questions.prompt: An attacker steals an authorization code from a PKCE S256 flow but does not know the verifier. Why should the token endpoint reject the exchange?

sources.title: RFC 7636: Proof Key for Code Exchange by OAuth Public Clients
sources.claim: PKCE requires the matching verifier at redemption. A stolen code alone is insufficient. The code is not an encrypted password, and the challenge is not a reusable token.

questions.explanation: PKCE requires the matching verifier at redemption. A stolen code alone is insufficient. The code is not an encrypted password, and the challenge is not a reusable token.

choices.text: The authorization code becomes an encrypted password that only the browser can decrypt.
The token endpoint needs no proof because an intercepted code is never usable.
The attacker cannot supply the verifier matching the saved challenge.
The challenge is a reusable access token that must replace the authorization code.

questions.prompt: An Express app must verify Stripe webhook signatures while other routes accept parsed JSON. What should the webhook path preserve for verification?

sources.title: Stripe: Receive Stripe events in your webhook endpoint
sources.claim: Signature verification needs the raw body, so arrange webhook middleware to preserve it before transformations. Re-serialization, field extraction and sorting do not preserve the original signed bytes.

questions.explanation: Signature verification needs the raw body, so arrange webhook middleware to preserve it before transformations. Re-serialization, field extraction and sorting do not preserve the original signed bytes.

choices.text: A newly serialized object after global JSON middleware has transformed it.
Only the event id and type extracted from the globally parsed JSON object.
A sorted JSON object that replaces the original whitespace and field ordering.
The original request payload before JSON middleware transforms it.

questions.prompt: A team increases its password-hashing work factor as hardware improves. Which upgrade statements follow OWASP guidance? Select all that apply.

sources.title: OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet
sources.claim: A: higher work factors make hashing more expensive. C: successful authentication provides the password needed to compute an upgraded hash. B is false because old hashes remain unchanged. D and E ignore resource exhaustion, hardware differences and measured verification latency.

questions.explanation: A: higher work factors make hashing more expensive. C: successful authentication provides the password needed to compute an upgraded hash. B is false because old hashes remain unchanged. D and E ignore resource exhaustion, hardware differences and measured verification latency.

choices.text: Higher work factors increase the cost of each password guess.
Every stored hash changes automatically when the application setting increases.
Rehash a password after a successful login when its stored factor is outdated.
Choose unlimited cost because password verification cannot affect availability.
Choose the same work factor for every server without measuring its verification cost.
